purpose: Original conceptual editorial illustrations, not data or anatomical/experimental schematics

images.prompt: Create a refined editorial science illustration for a long-form physics review, widescreen 16:9. A precisely focused warm near-infrared laser pulse crosses a thin cool X-ray probe in an evacuated interaction chamber; after the crossing, the probe's polarization is suggested by two delicately separated luminous ribbon orientations. Sparse optomechanical forms, dark midnight teal space, warm copper and ivory light, restrained hand-painted technical illustration texture. The invisible vacuum response is an artistic metaphor, not a real image or an exact apparatus. Scientifically avoid particles popping out as literal objects, cosmic planets, circuit boards, robots, and labels. No text, letters, numbers, logos, graphs, or watermarks. Compose a clear focal interaction with generous breathing room, professional magazine quality. Landscape 1536x864 intent.

Create an original editorial illustration for a physics review about reconstructing quantum spin correlations from particle collider decay data. Landscape 16:9. A cutaway cylindrical high-energy particle detector, with two elegant opposing sprays of tracks emerging from one central collision, their angular patterns visually echoed in two small abstract translucent paired probability forms. Sophisticated ink and soft gouache texture, ivory paper, navy, petrol teal, restrained warm gold, crisp elegant editorial composition. This is a conceptual illustration, not actual experimental event data: no exact track labels, no numbers, no charts, no claims of a detected dark matter particle. No entanglement communication beam joining separated objects, no robots, generic computer chips, text, logos or watermark.

Create a sophisticated editorial science illustration about mathematical singularity in a viscous fluid and computer-assisted proof. Widescreen 16:9. A flowing three-dimensional vortex tube narrows toward a tiny central region while being stretched axially, represented by many fine navy and teal streamlines with amber accents, beside a quiet stack-like arrangement of abstract translucent mathematical construction sheets with no writing. Strong visual focus on concentrated fluid motion; balanced cream paper backdrop, printmaking and precise gouache style. Conceptual artwork only, not a numerical simulation and not a physical explosion. Avoid equations, axes, numbers, words, logos, robots, circuit boards, glowing AI brains, chaotic decorative shapes. Professional science magazine composition.

Create a respectful original editorial neuroscience illustration, widescreen 16:9, for a review of how peripheral facial sensory nerve stimulation might influence memory circuits. Show an adult human head in a gentle three-quarter profile, simplified translucent anatomy with fine branching facial sensory nerves and a softly outlined brainstem leading to distributed brain regions. Small subtle skin-surface contacts may be suggested but do not specify placement or show a usable medical device. Precise restrained ink-and-gouache style on warm ivory background, muted teal nerves, navy anatomical outline, small amber accents. Conceptual not anatomically exact medical guidance. No lightning bolts, no pain, no treatment claims, no child, no realistic patient, no equations, words, numbers, logo, watermark or digital AI circuitry.

Create a compact editorial environmental science illustration, widescreen 16:9, about El Nino and the vulnerability of Amazon rainforest to heat and drying. An expansive winding Amazon river through dense canopy with some gently drying forest edges under a warm hazy sky; a restrained atmospheric sweep in the sky alludes to distant Pacific influence without drawing a geographical map or quantitative weather data. Elegant flat gouache and fine ink texture on ivory, forest teal, ochre, burnt sienna. Show ecological vulnerability, not an apocalyptic fire or a confirmed prediction. No text, numbers, graph, map boundaries, logos or watermark.
